::: {#rem-architectures}

#### Some convolutional networks that changed the field

- LeNet-5 read handwritten digits with two [convolutional layers](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#def-convolutional-layer),
  each followed by subsampling,
  then [fully connected](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/neural-nets.html#def-fully-connected) layers [@lecun1998gradient].
  `make_cnn()` follows the same plan at a smaller size.
- AlexNet won the 2012 ImageNet competition with 5 convolutional layers,
  [ReLU](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-relu) activations,
  [dropout](regularization.qmd#def-dropout)
  and training on GPUs [@krizhevsky2012imagenet].
- VGG networks stacked $3 \times 3$ convolutional layers,
  16 or 19 weight layers in all [@simonyan2015vgg],
  for the reasons in @sol-two-small-filters.
- ResNets added [residual connections](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/backpropagation.html#def-residual-connection) around pairs or triples of convolutional layers,
  and trained networks of more than 100 layers [@he2016resnet].
  The [normalization chapter](normalization.qmd#rem-residual-block) used residual connections around single fully connected layers.

:::
